topIssues.title: Kona frame parsing mismatch against op-node and OP Stack Specs
topIssues.author: kevin-valerio
topIssues.body:
## Bug description

The [OP Stack derivation spec defines](https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/derivation.html#:~:text=is_last%20is%20a%20single%20byte%20with%20a%20value%20of%201%20if%20the%20frame%20is%20the%20last%20in%20the%20channel%2C%200%20if%20there%20are%20frames%20in%20the%20channel.%20Any%20other%20value%20makes%20the%20frame%20invalid%20(it%20must%20be%20ignored%20by%20the%20rollup%20node).) `is_last` as a byte that must be 0 or 1 and any other value makes the frame invalid and it must be ignored by the rollup node. The same spec [also](https://specs.optimism.io/protocol/derivation.html#:~:text=All%20frames%20in%20a%20batcher%20transaction%20must%20be%20parseable.%20If%20any%20one%20frame%20fails%20to%20parse%2C%20the%20all%20frames%20in%20the%20transaction%20are%20rejected.) states that all frames in a batcher transaction must be parseable, and if any frame fails to parse, then all frames in that transaction are rejected.

However, the `kona-protocol` frame decoder accepts invalid `is_last` bytes, while `op-node` rejects them. This parsing mismatch can make the Rust pipeline accept L1 batch inbox data that op-node rejects. If a system uses both implementations (for example a node in Go and a proof program in Rust), it can cause client disagreement and different L2 inputs.

On the Go side, op-node implements properly the spec: Frame.UnmarshalBinary returns an error for any `is_last` other than 0 or 1. However, on the Rust side (Kona), `Frame::decode` currently treats `is_last` as (byte == 1), meaning invalid values like 2 are accepted as false instead of being rejected.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2eb7e3c074b6b77cf94956529508ec882b0b5f18/op-node/rollup/derive/frame.go#L105-L107

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2eb7e3c074b6b77cf94956529508ec882b0b5f18/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/frame.rs#L210-L212

## Impact Details
If a Kona-based proof path is used to judge claims (CANNON_KONA as the used game type), it can validate an output root claim that does not match the spec and op-node which can cause an incorrect dispute outcome. Noting that with [upgrade 18](https://docs.optimism.io/notices/upgrade-18) which adds CANNON_KONA (8) with CANNON (0) to add Kona's fault proof path to run with the Go path, chains can have CANNON_KONA (8) becomes the respected game type, making this bug production ready.

## Risk

A serialization bug in the batcher service writes is_last = 2 for frame 0 of a channel, while the rest of the frame fields are correct. The batcher posts two L1 transactions to the batch inbox: the first contains frame 0 with is_last = 2 (instead of 0), and the second contains frame 1 with is_last = 1. A Go op-node rejects the first transaction during frame parsing (invalid is_last), and per spec the transaction’s frames are rejected, so it cannot assemble the channel from the second transaction alone.

A Rust kona pipeline accepts the first transaction, treats is_last = 2 as false, and assembles a complete channel after ingesting the second transaction. If the channel bytes decompress and decode into batches, the Rust fault proof program derives an output root that differs from the spec/Go output root for the same L1 head, and the system can reach a state where the fault proof program and op-node disagree on whether an output root claim is valid.

## Fix
The fix is straight-forward, validate that is_last is either 0 or 1 during frame decoding, and reject any other value, so it matches the spec and op-node.

## Author notes
This bug was initially reported in Immunefi but closed since considered as out-of-scope. These bugs were found using a differential fuzzing approach and [gosentry](https://github.com/kevin-valerio/gosentry).

topIssues.title: Unknown batch type panics and causes denial of service in kona-protocol
topIssues.author: kevin-valerio
topIssues.body:
## Bug description
The `kona-protocol` batch decoder panics when it reads an unknown batch type byte, letting malformed batch data crashing the node that decodes OP Stack batches.

The batch type is encoded as the first byte of the batch. The `BatchType` conversion uses `impl From<u8>` and calls `panic!` for any value other than `0x00` (single batch) or `0x01` (span batch).
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/batch/type.rs#L31-L39

This behavior diverges from the Go `op-node` implementation, which treats unknown batch types as decode errors and lets the derivation pipeline continue.
https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/op-node/rollup/derive/batch.go#L135-L137

The OP Stack specification defines the batch format as a version byte followed by content and states that unknown versions make the batch invalid and must be ignored by the rollup node. A panic violates this requirement because it stops the process instead of rejecting and skipping the invalid batch.

This issue is more impactful when building long-running services such as `kona-node`. Several Rust workspace profiles set `panic = "abort"`, which makes any reachable panic abort the process.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/rust/Cargo.toml#L194-L199

The main security risk here is a pure node software crash and a denial-of-service, given the Cargo.toml configuration, as well as a spec divergence.

## Risk
An operator runs `kona-node` as a service and builds it with a profile that sets `panic = "abort"` (one of the profile already present). A bug in the batcher submits a batch transaction whose first byte is `0x67`. The `BatchType` conversion panics and the process aborts.

## Author notes
This bug was initially reported in Immunefi but closed since considered as out-of-scope. These bugs were found using a differential fuzzing approach and [gosentry](https://github.com/kevin-valerio/gosentry).

topIssues.title: Kona and op-node can disagree on brotli channels
topIssues.author: kevin-valerio
topIssues.body:
## Bugs description
This issue actually contains two distinct bugs that can cause divergence between Kona and op-node for brotli-compressed channels.

- Bug 1: `decompress_brotli` can return `Ok()` even when brotli decompression did **not** reach `ResultSuccess`.
- Bug 2: Kona selects brotli based on the leading version byte and only later gates Fjord using `batch.timestamp`. op-node gates brotli **up front** using the L1 inclusion context (`isFjord`).

If a system uses Kona in a fault proof program / dispute game, these divergences can lead to incorrect outputs becoming accepted on Kona, while being refused on op-node. 

### `decompress_brotli` returns `Ok()` without requiring `ResultSuccess`

`decompress_brotli` loops only while the decoder returns `NeedsMoreOutput`. If the decoder returns `NeedsMoreInput` or `ResultFailure`, the loop stops and the function still returns `Ok(output_truncated_to_written_bytes)`.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/brotli.rs#L44-L73

Kona can treat invalid or truncated brotli as "valid decompressed bytes" (even if potentially empty), returning `Ok(vec![])` or `Ok(partial_bytes)`. The function only errors when the output would exceed `max_rlp_bytes_per_channel` (`BatchTooLarge`).

This is a divergence against op-node behavior that streams decompression through `brotli.NewReader(...)` and propagate errors during RLP decode if the brotli stream is truncated or invalid.

###  Fjord brotli gating is checked too late and uses a different time basis
In Kona, `BatchReader::decompress` decides "this is brotli" from the first byte (`CHANNEL_VERSION_BROTLI == 1`) and then decompresses the rest. `BatchReader::next_batch` only rejects brotli *after* decoding a batch, by checking Fjord using `cfg.is_fjord_active(batch.timestamp())`.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/batch/reader.rs#L95-L98


https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/batch/reader.rs#L117-L120

However, in op-node, brotli is gated **up front** using the L1 inclusion context (`isFjord`). If it’s not Fjord, op-node rejects brotli immediately.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/op-node/rollup/derive/channel.go#L193-L197

Kona and op-node can disagree on whether brotli is acceptable around Fjord, because Kona’s check is based on **`batch.timestamp()` (L2 data)** and happens **after** decompression+decode, while op-node’s check is based on the **L1 inclusion context** and happens **before** setting up the brotli reader.
 
### Risk for the truncated brotli stream being accepted by Kona (bug 1)
A buggy authorized batch submitter sends an L1 batch inbox transaction whose channel starts with the brotli version byte `0x01`. An actor crafts a brotli stream that starts decompressing into a valid RLP-encoded batch, then truncates the brotli data so the decoder ends in `NeedsMoreInput` (not `ResultSuccess`). `op-node` brotli is streamed via `brotli.NewReader`, and the RLP decode fails due to invalid decompression. Kona `decompress_brotli` returns `Ok(partial_bytes)` and the batch decode can succeed from those bytes. Kona derives a different output than op-node. 

### Risk for pre-Fjord inclusion but post-Fjord batch timestamp (bug 2)
Assume `fjord_time = 2_000`. An actor submits a brotli channel (first byte `0x01`) in an L1 inclusion context with `origin.timestamp = 1_999` (pre-Fjord). The decoded batch inside the channel uses `batch.timestamp = 2_000` (Fjord-active by timestamp). `op-node`'s `isFjord == false` based on L1 inclusion context, so brotli is rejected immediately. 

However brotli decompression runs, the batch is decoded, and the Fjord check uses `cfg.is_fjord_active(batch.timestamp()) == true`, so the batch can be accepted. Kona accepts brotli data that op-node rejects, again creating derivation divergence risk.

### Fix for the first bug
Change `decompress_brotli` to return an error unless `BrotliDecompressStream()` reaches `BrotliResult::ResultSuccess`. Handle `NeedsMoreInput` and `ResultFailure` as errors, not as "success with partial output".

### Fix for the second bug
Gate brotli before decompression using the L1 inclusion context, as op-node’s `isFjord` is doing. Pass an `is_fjord`/`origin_timestamp` decision into the Kona `BatchReader` and reject brotli channels pre-Fjord.

## Author notes
This bug was initially reported in Immunefi but closed since considered as out-of-scope. These bugs were found using a differential fuzzing approach and [gosentry](https://github.com/kevin-valerio/gosentry).
